excluded: Physical equilibrium qualification from arbitrary matrix use

example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.electromagnetism import get_gpsi
R,Z=np.meshgrid([.4,.8,1.2],[-.5,0.,.9])
G=get_gpsi(R,Z)
assert G.shape==(9,9) and np.all(np.diag(G)==0)
example.description: Build an irregular three-row node response.
example.expected: Dense finite matrix with explicit zero-self diagonal.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for malformed, complex, nonfinite or negative-radius geometry and duplicate active pairs.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Kernel FloatingPointError propagates on unrepresentable output.

assumptions: Coordinates are finite real arrays; output is dense O(N^2).
identity.boundary: Axis target flux and zero-radius source flux are zero. Diagonal exactly zero. Distinct positive-radius coincident entries reject.
identity.coordinates: R,Z in m; source column current in A; G in Wb/rad/A.
identity.definition: psi_i=sum_j G_ij I_j with psi=R A_phi. Flattening is C-order. The predecessor reflected shifted row blocks, valid only on equal Z spacing and identical R rows; this successor evaluates actual pair geometry.
identity.direction: Matching planar R,Z node arrays to a target/source flux matrix
identity.geometry: Finite arbitrary 2-D cylindrical node arrays; nonnegative R.
identity.model: Vacuum ideal circular filaments with retained zero-self discrete quadrature, not finite-wire inductance.
identity.relation: G_ij = (mu0/(4pi)) a_j R_i integral cos(phi)/sqrt((R_i-a_j)^2+4 R_i a_j sin(phi/2)^2+(Z_i-Z_j)^2) dphi for i != j; G_ii=0.

outputs.description: Flux response matrix with target rows/source columns
outputs.name: G
